title: CMTS: A Conditional Multiple Trajectory Synthesizer for Generating Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios

control_signal.value: Road map (binary grid image) as condition, plus an interpolation weight lambda between safe-data and collision-data latent codes; lambda is fixed (0.3 in the Argoverse experiment) at generation to get near-miss samples.

control_mechanism.value: Safe and collision latents are linearly interpolated (lambda sampled uniformly in training); road map is injected as a style via AdaIN on the latent; a consistency regularizer supports the fused samples.

base_model.value: Conditional VAE: GRU trajectory encoder, convolutional map encoder producing Gaussian style statistics, GRU decoder that generates trajectories.

datasets.value: Argoverse motion forecasting (two interacting vehicles plus maps; collision set built by translating trajectories to a collision point), Lines dataset, MNIST and USPS.

metrics.value: DPGMM cluster number K as dataset complexity; trajectory prediction MSE; minimal distance between vehicles (MDV) as risk; mean distance between neighbour waypoints (MDN) as smoothness; Smoothness and Mean Distance on Lines.

controllability_evidence.value: Augmented set has more clusters: K=71±11 for CMTS vs 64±7 original; OD+CMTS reaches 127±20. Training prediction models on CMTS data gives best MSE, MDV, MDN (e.g. CS-LSTM MSE 0.042 vs 0.048 on original).

stated_limitations.value: No physical or kinematic constraints were applied to generated trajectories, which would make them closer to real ones; planned as future work.

notes: Primarily a data-augmentation method for trajectory prediction; control is only via road map condition and a fixed interpolation coefficient, no direct test that lambda monotonically sets criticality in the packet.
